tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Orientation for these tools plus a workspace map (spaces → databases → fields). Without `section` it returns the overview and an index of section names; with `section` it returns one reference section (FILTERS, ICONS, WORKING NOTES, TOOL NOTES <tool>).

workspace.description: Workspace name or id to map (optional).

section.description: Optional. One section name from the index this tool returns when called without it, e.g. 'TOOL NOTES create_automation', 'FILTERS', 'ICONS'. Exact name first, then case-insensitive. Omit for the overview and the index.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: Every workspace the token can access (id, name, role, description).

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: One workspace, addressed directly by name/slug/id — its full metadata, including settings.

workspace.description: Workspace name, slug, or id (from list_workspaces).

tools.name: list_databases
tools.description: Databases in a workspace. `ref` is the canonical space/database slug, which identifies one database unambiguously; a bare name can be ambiguous because the same name can exist in two spaces.

tools.name: describe_database
tools.description: The schema of one database: every field with its exact api_name, type, select options and relation targets. These are the exact api_names that record writes and queries are keyed by.

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Full-text search records across a workspace by title. Turns a name ("the Acme project") into a real record id.

tools.name: count_records
tools.description: Count records in a database, or total/average a numeric field — computed in the database, returning one number. Answers "how many" questions exactly: the count is made in the database, whereas counting the results of query_records, which is paginated, gives the size of one page, not the total. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES count_records"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

op.description: Default "count". The others need `field` and aggregate its numeric values.

field.description: Field api_name to aggregate. Required for everything except count.

filter.description: Same filter AST as query_records. See also: get_started section "FILTERS".

q.description: Free-text match on the title, same as query_records.

tools.name: count_records_grouped
tools.description: Count records (or total/average/min/max a numeric field) PER GROUP of another field, in one call — computed in the database. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES count_records_grouped"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

group_by.description: Field api_name to group by — see the type list above.

group_by_granularity.description: Required when group_by is a date field; ignored otherwise. Each group's key is that bucket's start date.

op.description: Default "count". The others need `field` and aggregate its numeric values within each group.

field.description: Field api_name to aggregate. Required for everything except count.

filter.description: Same filter AST as query_records. See also: get_started section "FILTERS".

q.description: Free-text match on the title, same as query_records.

tools.name: query_records
tools.description: List/filter/sort records in a database. filter is the structured AST (See also: get_started section "FILTERS" for the full op cheat-sheet). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES query_records"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

filter.description: Filter AST — grouped { and: [{ field, op, value }] }/{ or: [...] }, or a bare { field, op, value } condition. Example: { "field": "priority", "op": "eq", "value": "Urgent" }. See also: get_started section "FILTERS" for the op-by-field-type cheat sheet.

sorts.description: Sort keys by field api_name. A select or workflow field sorts by its OPTION ORDER (the order the field's options are arranged in: Low → Urgent, Triage → Done), not alphabetically by label; desc reverses it. A multi_select sorts by the position of its FIRST stored value. Records with no value come last.

view.description: View id or name — applies that view's saved filter and sorts, so "the records in this view" matches what the UI shows. A `view` URL's ?view=<uuid> works directly. Your own `filter`/`sorts` override the view's.

tools.name: get_record
tools.description: One record in full — values keyed by api_name, resolved relation chips. Accepts the record uuid or its public number. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_record"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

tools.name: create_record
tools.description: Create a record. values are keyed by api_name (field names as listed by describe_database); select/person values accept the human label, rich_text accepts Markdown, and relation fields accept an array of target record numbers or ids — linked in the same write, so no follow-up link_records. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_record"]

values.description: Field values by api_name; "name" sets the title. A relation field takes an array of target record numbers or ids, e.g. { project: [12] } — created atomically with the record.

tools.name: upsert_record
tools.description: #230: match-or-create on a unique key. key_field must be a field marked unique via update_field/add_field's unique config (#229). values must include key_field — that value is the match. A matching record is updated (merge, same as update_record); no match creates a new record. Returns { record, created }, so a caller can tell which branch it took.

key_field.description: api_name of the unique field to match on.

values.description: Field values by api_name; must include key_field. Relation fields work the same as create_record.

tools.name: update_record
tools.description: Merge-update a record (null clears a field). values by api_name; record is a uuid or public number. Fields marked read_only in describe_database (system columns, and on an agent run its pending_action, run_class and cost, which the agent runtime owns) cannot be written and are refused. Returns the updated record.

tools.name: get_record_description
tools.description: The record's own rich-text description/document — the block editor content shown under its title, NOT a custom field literally named "description" (such a field appears in get_record's values, if the database has one). Returns Markdown. version 0 means it has never been written.

tools.name: update_record_description
tools.description: Overwrite the record's rich-text description/document — the block editor content shown under its title, NOT a custom field literally named "description" (that field is set through update_record's values). content is Markdown (headings/lists/links parsed into real blocks, same as a rich_text field). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES update_record_description"]

content.description: Markdown. An empty string clears the description.

expected_version.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard. Omit to overwrite regardless of the current version.

tools.name: delete_record
tools.description: Move a record to trash (restorable 30 days). record is a uuid or public number.

tools.name: link_records
tools.description: Link a record through a relation field to target records (by uuid or public number). Default ADDS links; `replace: true` sets the link set to exactly `targets`, which is how a one-to-many link is re-pointed or cleared (adding a second target without replace returns a 409). Target ids come from search / query_records.

relation_field.description: The relation field on this database (api_name, name, or id).

targets.description: Target record uuids or public numbers. With replace:true, an empty array clears all links.

replace.description: Replace the whole link set with `targets` instead of adding to it — required to change a one-to-many link (#81).

tools.name: unlink_records
tools.description: Remove specific links from a record's relation field, leaving the relation and every other link intact. Fixes a mis-link (link_records with replace does too); unlike delete_relation, which drops the relation everywhere, it touches only the named links (#81).

relation_field.description: The relation field on this database (api_name, name, or id).

targets.description: Target record uuids or public numbers to unlink.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Post a plain-text comment on a record (uuid or public number).

tools.name: list_trash
tools.description: The deleted records of a database, newest first — restorable for 30 days, then gone for good. A deleted record no longer resolves by public number anywhere else, so this is where the ids restore_records takes come from; it also shows whether a delete took effect.

tools.name: delete_records
tools.description: Move up to 200 records to trash in one call (restorable 30 days via list_trash / restore_records). Records are uuids or public numbers. Exists so cleaning up a query result is one call instead of two hundred; delete_record handles a single one.

tools.name: restore_records
tools.description: Bring records back from the trash. Pass uuids or public numbers — a number is resolved against the trash listing, since a deleted record no longer resolves by number anywhere else. Restoring one record returns the record; restoring several returns a count.

records.description: Record uuids or public numbers (see list_trash).

tools.name: duplicate_record
tools.description: Copy a record: its values, its description document, and its single/many-to-many links. Owned collections (the "many" side a record owns) are NOT copied — a duplicated project does not clone its tasks. Returns the new record, which makes it a template-instantiation step (a filled-in record need not be re-typed).

tools.name: copy_records
tools.description: #521 — copy one or more records into a DIFFERENT database (unlike duplicate_record, which copies within the same one). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES copy_records"]

database.description: Source database.

records.description: Record uuids or public numbers to copy.

skip.description: Source field api_names to skip explicitly — resolves a blocking field.

override.description: Source field api_name -> destination field id (from a dry_run plan's own field ids, or an ambiguousWith candidate's field_id). Wins over auto-match and resolves an ambiguous relation by naming the exact one to use.

dry_run.description: Default true: preview the mapping and any blocking fields without writing anything.

tools.name: move_record
tools.description: Reposition a record in the hand-arranged (manual) order — the order list_records returns and a board/list shows. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES move_record"]

before.description: Land immediately BEFORE this record (uuid or public number).

after.description: Land immediately AFTER this record (uuid or public number).

values.description: Optional field patch applied atomically with the move — the column a kanban card is dropped into.

tools.name: list_records
tools.description: Records in the hand-arranged (drag) order a human sees — the one thing query_records cannot express, since it sorts by field values and falls back to manual order only when given no sorts at all. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_records"]

q.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the record title.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: Read a record's comment thread, newest first, as plain text — including the ones you posted with add_comment. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_comments"]

tools.name: list_database_comments
tools.description: Every comment AND #record reference across every record in a database, newest first — a quick "what happened recently" overview, without visiting each record. Different from list_comments, which reads ONE record's thread; this is the cross-record feed. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_database_comments"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

tools.name: list_hierarchy_activity
tools.description: Comments AND #record references across a whole relation TREE rooted at one record — e.g. every comment/reference on an Epic AND its Stories AND their Tasks, not just the Epic itself. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_hierarchy_activity"]

database.description: The ROOT record's database — name, api slug, or id.

record.description: The ROOT record — number or id.

database.description: The database THIS level's relation field lives on (the previous level's target database; for level 1, the root's own database).

field.description: Relation field name, api_name, or id on that database.

relation_fields.description: One entry per level, e.g. [{database: "Epics", field: "Stories"}, {database: "Stories", field: "Tasks"}] to walk Epic → Story → Task.

tools.name: update_comment
tools.description: Replace the text of a comment you authored (id from list_comments). Editing someone else's is refused by the API; an edit replaces the text in place, so the thread holds one comment, not a correction after the original.

body.description: The replacement text — replaces the whole comment, not appended.

tools.name: delete_comment
tools.description: Delete a comment you authored (workspace admins may delete any). The id comes from list_comments. Unlike a record, a comment does not go to a trash you can browse — deleting is the end of it.

tools.name: get_history
tools.description: What happened to a record, newest first, through one of four lenses (`kind`): "fields" (default; per-field changes with before/after, for "who changed the status and when"), "versions" (whole-record snapshots; a version id goes to restore_version), "activity" (the full trail including comments, links and attachments) and "document_versions" (snapshots of the description document; an id goes to restore_document_version). Each lens answers a different question. Every row carries `source` (human/agent/automation/mcp). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_history"]

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Roll a record back to a previously captured snapshot. The version id comes from get_history with kind:"versions". This OVERWRITES the current values with the old ones and is itself recorded as a new version, so it is undoable. A snapshot list carries titles and timestamps, not values.

tools.name: restore_document_version
tools.description: #677 — roll a record's DESCRIPTION document back to a previously captured version. The version id comes from get_history with kind:"document_versions". Separate from restore_version, which only ever touches field values, never the description. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES restore_document_version"]

tools.name: list_backlinks
tools.description: Records whose description document MENTIONS this record — the "Mentioned in" list. This is prose cross-referencing, NOT relation links (structural links appear in get_record, and describe_database lists the relation fields). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_backlinks"]

tools.name: list_linked_records
tools.description: The full link set of ONE relation field on a record, as records you can act on (id, public number, title, url). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_linked_records"]

relation_field.description: The relation field on this database (api_name, name, or id).

tools.name: list_watchers
tools.description: Who gets notified when this record changes, and whether the caller is among them. A record with no watchers notifies nobody except through an explicit mention.

tools.name: watch_record
tools.description: Subscribe (or unsubscribe) the CALLING identity to a record's changes. Note what this is not: it cannot subscribe someone else — a token watches on behalf of whoever it belongs to. Mentioning a person in add_comment is how a record is brought to someone else's attention.

watch.description: true (default) to watch, false to stop watching.

tools.name: attach_file
tools.description: Attach a file to a record — either from a public `url` (fetched by the StoryOS server, which refuses private/internal addresses and caps the size) or from inline `content_base64` bytes. Images get a thumbnail automatically. record is a uuid or public number. Returns the created attachment.

url.description: A publicly reachable URL to fetch and attach.

content_base64.description: Base64-encoded file bytes (use instead of url).

filename.description: File name — required with content_base64; inferred from the URL otherwise.

mime.description: MIME type, e.g. "image/png". Inferred from the extension / URL response when omitted.

field.description: An attachment FIELD to put the file in (name or id), instead of the record-level bag. For a record with a "Cover"/"Video" style column: a gallery card renders the FIRST file of its cover field, so upload order is the order they appear.

tools.name: list_attachments
tools.description: List the files attached to a record (id, filename, mime, size). record is a uuid or public number.

tools.name: delete_attachment
tools.description: Remove a file from a record by attachment id (from list_attachments). record is a uuid or public number.

tools.name: run_button
tools.description: Press a button field on a record, running its configured actions (set values / create linked / comment / notify / update linked).

button.description: The button field (api_name, name, or id).

tools.name: propose_schema
tools.description: Turn a plain-language goal ("track clients, their projects and invoices") into a PLAN — databases, fields, relations and states, each marked create-new or reuse-existing. Creates NOTHING; the plan is the input build_schema takes. This is the fast path for building a workspace (one call replaces one add_field per field).

goal.description: What the workspace is for, in plain language.

mode.description: Omit for the free deterministic planner. "storyos_ai" is metered against this workspace's AI credits.

tools.name: build_schema
tools.description: Build an approved plan from propose_schema in ONE call — every database, field, relation and state together, reusing existing databases where the plan says reuse. Returns a summary of what was created vs reused, with ids. Replaces a sequence of create_database/add_field calls.

plan.description: The plan object returned by propose_schema, passed back verbatim.

tools.name: list_packs
tools.description: The built-in Business Pack gallery — ready-made workspaces (databases, fields, relations, views, sample data). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_packs"]

tools.name: install_pack
tools.description: Install a Business Pack by slug (from list_packs): creates its databases, fields, relations and views in one call. Idempotent. `preview: true` reports, changing nothing, per database create / reuse / collision and what it would add. Automations that send anything outside the workspace or run an agent, and state-bound agent triggers, install SWITCHED OFF: name them in enable_automations / enable_agent_triggers to switch one on. A failed install rolls back everything that request installed. Covers reuse_databases, required_packs, update_agents, existing_elsewhere, scheduled pack agents. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES install_pack"]

preview.description: Show what would be created and create nothing; on a workspace that already has data the report says per database whether it is reused or collides.

space.description: Install INTO this existing space (name, slug or id from list_spaces), not into a space of the pack's own: every database, view and automation lands in it and no space is created. Only for a pack whose databases all sit in one space; a multi-space pack is refused, and so is one whose databases already exist in a different space. You need edit access to the space; a personal space is refused. Omit it for the usual install. Works with preview, which reports the outcome without installing.

update_agents.description: Names of installed agents a person EDITED whose content should be replaced with this pack version (preview marks them agent_update.status = edited_needs_choice). Agents not named stay as they are.

enable_automations.description: Labels ("Database.Rule name", as preview lists them) of automations that send something outside the workspace (email, Slack, webhook, HTTP, social post) or run an agent, which a pack installs SWITCHED OFF, that you want switched ON. Only name one when the person asked for it; a pack's own enabled:true on such a rule is ignored. Preview and the install result list every automation with enabled / enabled_on_install and, when off for what it does, switched_off_because.

reuse_databases.description: Reuse an EXISTING database instead of creating the pack's own, with the id naming WHICH one when several share that name: {"Issues": "<database id>"}. The id must be one of the `existing_elsewhere.candidates` the preview lists for that database (editable by you, reusable: true); a database synced from Linear, a built-in one, a personal-space one, one you cannot edit or one the pack does not fit is refused with the reason. Without it, a database name that exists once elsewhere is not reused (preview says why), and with several the install stops at the ambiguity.

enable_agent_triggers.description: Labels ("Agent ← Database.Field = State", exactly as preview lists them under `triggers`) of state-bound agent triggers, which a pack installs SWITCHED OFF, that you want switched ON (the agent then wakes by itself whenever a record reaches that state). Only name one when the person asked for it; a pack cannot switch one on itself. Has no effect on a trigger that already exists.

required_packs.description: For a pack that builds on another pack (preview `required_packs`): {"<pack slug>": "also_install" | "create_here"}. also_install installs that built-in pack first and links to its databases; create_here makes the linked databases inside this pack (the default when the other pack is not installed; when it IS installed the databases are linked unless you say create_here). Only name one when the person chose it.

tools.name: create_records
tools.description: Create up to 100 records in ONE atomic call — all succeed or none do. Values are keyed by api_name exactly as create_record takes them. Replaces calling create_record in a loop. If a gate on this agent holds creates, the whole batch is held as one approval and the response is { pending_approval, approval_id } with nothing created.

tools.name: update_records
tools.description: Apply ONE set of values to up to 200 records at once — the "set status to Done for everything in this view" shape. Partial failures are reported per record rather than failing the whole call; records whose update a gate on this agent held for approval are listed in `held` ({record_id, approval_id}) and were NOT changed. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES update_records"]

values.description: The patch applied to every listed record.

tools.name: undo_batch_update
tools.description: Revert a prior update_records call using the `restorable` list from ITS response — pass that array back verbatim. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES undo_batch_update"]

restorable.description: The `restorable` array from a prior update_records response.

tools.name: enqueue_bulk_record_job
tools.description: For a selection bigger than update_records/delete_records can take in one call (over 5000 ids): runs as a durable, chunked, resumable background job instead of one request. Returns immediately with a job id — poll get_bulk_record_job with it to see progress. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES enqueue_bulk_record_job"]

values.description: Required when op is "update"; omit for "delete".

tools.name: get_bulk_record_job
tools.description: Status and progress for a job from enqueue_bulk_record_job — total/processed/succeeded, any per-record failures, and (for an update job) the restorable list for undo_batch_update once it settles.

tools.name: create_database
tools.description: Create a new database (table) in a space. Returns it with its auto-created system fields (id, name). Shaped further with add_field and create_view.

space.description: Space name or id the database belongs to. Never a personal space: those hold documents and views only (422).

icon.description: A curated icon ref, e.g. "set:rocket" or a brand/logo ref like "brand:github" (#298). See also: get_started section "ICONS" for the full catalog. A raw emoji (e.g. "📁") still works for backward compatibility with older data, but is not the preferred form.

color.description: Palette colour: gray, brown, gold, orange, red, pink, purple, blue, teal, green, lime, cyan, indigo, magenta, rose. Omit on create and one is auto-assigned AT RANDOM, so databases created in a row can end up sharing a colour (two purples).

description.description: One line (max 200 chars) saying what this is FOR — read by list_* and describe_database, so it becomes context for whoever works here next. Set it when you create something: you already know the purpose at that moment.

tools.name: preview_formula
tools.description: Dry-run a formula without saving it (add_field and update_field are what save one): checks `expression` against the database's fields and evaluates it on up to 5 recent records. Saves NOTHING. Returns valid, return_type, samples and positioned errors with a suggestion. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES preview_formula"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

expression.description: The formula, e.g. {Qty} * {Unit Price} or if({Status} = "Done", 1, 0).

field.description: An existing formula field (name, api_name or id) whose expression you are replacing.

samples.description: How many records to evaluate (default and maximum 5).

tools.name: add_field
tools.description: Add a field to a database. select/multi_select/workflow take options as labels; `workflow` is the type of the one lifecycle status field a database is tracked by (at most ONE; board grouping and My Work key off it), whereas `select` is an ordinary choice field. lookup/rollup/formula/ai need `config`; a formula can be checked with preview_formula, which saves nothing. Relations are not added here (create_relation adds them). Covers formula format and currency, rollup ops and filters, AI field prompt/output. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES add_field"]

options.description: select/multi_select/workflow choices, as labels or {label,color,icon,category}. On a workflow field each option gets a state category (inferred from its label and position unless you give one). Omit them on a workflow field to get To do / In progress / Done.

icon.description: Curated icon ref: "set:<name>" or "brand:<slug>" (See also: get_started section "ICONS").

category.description: State category: backlog | unstarted | started | completed | canceled (completed and canceled mean finished). Workflow options only (and select options that say it); inferred from the label when omitted on a workflow.

tools.name: update_field
tools.description: Rename a field, add select options, or edit and remove existing ones. Returns the updated field. Editing is non-destructive: recolouring or renaming an option leaves every record that holds it untouched, because options have stable ids and records point at the id, not the text. Removing one is the exception — it refuses with a usage count unless you confirm, and can reassign holders to another option.

field.description: Field to update (name, api_name, or id).

unique.description: #229 — mark a text/number field Unique (rejects a duplicate value on create/edit) or turn it off. Turning it on scans existing records first and refuses (naming the conflicting ones) instead of silently enabling.

unique_normalize.description: With `unique: true` — fold case and trim whitespace before comparing (default true).

add_options.description: New choices to add to a select/multi_select/workflow field. A workflow option's state category is inferred from its label unless you give one.

icon.description: Curated icon ref: "set:<name>" or "brand:<slug>" (See also: get_started section "ICONS").

category.description: State category: backlog | unstarted | started | completed | canceled (completed and canceled mean finished). Workflow options only (and select options that say it); inferred from the label when omitted on a workflow.

update_options.description: Recolour, rename or re-categorise EXISTING options. Records keep their values — ids are stable.

option.description: Existing option, by label or id.

color.description: New colour, from the option palette.

icon.description: Curated icon ref, or null to clear.

category.description: State category: backlog | unstarted | started | completed | canceled (completed and canceled mean finished). Workflow options only (and select options that say it); inferred from the label when omitted on a workflow. Pass null to clear it on a select option (a workflow option always keeps one).

remove_options.description: Delete options. Refuses with a usage count unless confirmed; the count is what confirming accepts.

option.description: Existing option, by label or id.

confirm.description: Required when records still use it. Without it you get a refusal naming the count.

reassign_to.description: Move holders onto this option instead of clearing them.

tools.name: get_field_usage
tools.description: What depends on this field, before you delete it: records carrying data in it, plus the views (filter/sort/group), automations (trigger/condition) and formulas that reference it. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_field_usage"]

tools.name: delete_field
tools.description: Soft-delete a field (records keep their other values). Returns records_with_value (records holding a non-empty value: blank, whitespace-only and never-set records are not counted). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES delete_field"]

tools.name: create_view
tools.description: Create a saved view. board needs group_by (a select, a single user, or a one-to-many relation field); calendar needs date_field; timeline needs start_date_field/end_date_field; board/gallery/list show card_fields (chips on calendar); form takes form_* to build the actual public-facing form (title/fields/access) — a bare "form" type with no form_* params creates an unconfigured, members-only form.

group_by.description: board: field to group columns by — a select, a single user, or the single side of a one-to-many relation (one column per related record).

hidden_columns.description: board (select/workflow group-by only): option LABELS (or ids) of columns NOT to draw, empty or not — e.g. ["Triage","Backlog","Done"]. Different from hiding empty columns. Pass [] to show every column again. Changing group_by without passing this clears it.

filters.description: Filter AST by field api_name — same shape as query_records (See also: get_started section "FILTERS").

form_title.description: form: heading shown to the visitor (defaults to the database name).

form_description.description: form: helper text shown under the title.

form_fields.description: form: which fields to show, in order — a field ref, or {field, required, label, help, visible_when, required_when, hidden, value} for per-field overrides. `hidden`+`value` stamps a fixed value onto every submission without ever showing that field to the visitor — a job/tenant id, a UTM tag. Omit to fall back to card_fields.

visible_when.description: #715 — show this field only when an earlier answer matches.

field.description: An EARLIER field in this same form (by name or id) whose answer controls this one.

value.description: Ignored by is_empty/not_empty. `in` takes an array.

required_when.description: #715 — `required` above only bites when this also holds (or is unset).

field.description: An EARLIER field in this same form (by name or id) whose answer controls this one.

value.description: Ignored by is_empty/not_empty. `in` takes an array.

tools.description: Rename a view or change its grouping / card fields / date fields / form config. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES update_view"]

hidden_columns.description: board (select/workflow group-by only): option LABELS (or ids) of columns NOT to draw, empty or not — e.g. ["Triage","Backlog","Done"]. Different from hiding empty columns. Pass [] to show every column again. Changing group_by without passing this clears it.

tools.name: delete_view
tools.description: #37 — soft delete: recoverable via restore_view (see list_views_trash). 409 if it is the last shared view on the database.

tools.name: list_views_trash
tools.description: #37 — deleted views on this database. A deleted view no longer resolves by name via list_views/get_database, so the ids restore_view takes are found here.

tools.name: restore_view
tools.description: #37 — bring a deleted view back (see list_views_trash for the id). Only for a view deleted on its own; a view that went with its whole database or space comes back with restore_database/restore_space.

view.description: View id (from list_views_trash) — a deleted view has no live name to resolve by.

tools.name: get_links
tools.description: Resolve web-app URLs — for records, a database, and/or its saved views — without a round-trip per record. get_record / query_records / create_record / update_record already include a `url` on each record; this tool returns a database link, a view link, or a batch of record links in one call.

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id. Required to resolve `records` or `views`; on its own, returns just the database link.

records.description: Record uuids or public numbers to link.

views.description: View names or ids to link.

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: The standalone documents in a space — the pages that live in the sidebar next to databases, belonging to no record. Titles and ids only; the text of one is returned by get_document.

space.description: Space name, slug, or id (from list_spaces).

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Read a standalone document as Markdown. `version` comes back with it; update_document accepts it to report a conflicting edit instead of silently overwriting someone.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Write a standalone page in a space — a summary, a plan, a write-up, meeting notes. A document is a page of prose; it is not a database and not the body of an unrelated record. `content` is Markdown (headings, lists, links, code). Optionally file it in a folder.

space.description: Space name, slug, or id (from list_spaces).

title.description: The page title, as it appears in the sidebar. Max 200 chars.

content.description: Markdown body. Omit for an empty page you will fill in later.

icon.description: A curated icon ref, e.g. "set:rocket" or a brand/logo ref like "brand:github" (#298). See also: get_started section "ICONS" for the full catalog. A raw emoji (e.g. "📁") still works for backward compatibility with older data, but is not the preferred form.

folder.description: Folder name or id to file it under (from list_folders).

tools.name: update_document
tools.description: Change a document's title, icon, folder, or body. `content` REPLACES the whole body, so it carries the full new text (as get_document returns it), not just the paragraph being added. Pass the `version` you read to be told about a conflicting edit (409) instead of overwriting it; omit it and the last write wins.

icon.description: A curated icon ref, e.g. "set:rocket" or a brand/logo ref like "brand:github" (#298). See also: get_started section "ICONS" for the full catalog. A raw emoji (e.g. "📁") still works for backward compatibility with older data, but is not the preferred form.

folder.description: Folder name or id, or null to move it to the space root.

version.description: The version from get_document. Omit to overwrite unconditionally.

tools.name: delete_document
tools.description: Delete a standalone document. Unlike a record this does not appear in any trash you can browse, so it is permanent.

confirm.description: Must be true — a title can resolve by exact match to the wrong page.

tools.name: move_document_to_space
tools.description: Move a document out of Personal into a shared space — a one-way publish (personal-space.md): the item becomes visible and exportable to everyone with access to the target space, and any @mentions in its body that were suppressed while it was personal now notify for the first time. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES move_document_to_space"]

space.description: The space the document is in now.

target_space.description: The shared space to move it into (from list_spaces). Must not be a personal space.

tools.name: copy_document_to_personal_space
tools.description: Fork a document you can see into your own Personal space — an independent copy, never synced back (personal-space.md's answer to "publishing is one-way"). Editing either copy afterward never touches the other.

space.description: The space the document is in now.

tools.name: list_folders
tools.description: The folders in a space — the sidebar groups that documents, databases and views can be filed under. These are the existing groups create_document's `folder` accepts, so a page can be filed in one instead of a near-duplicate being invented.

tools.name: create_folder
tools.description: Add a sidebar folder to a space. A folder is how a person finds several related things later. list_folders shows the existing ones; a second "Reports" next to an existing one is worse than no folder.

icon.description: A curated icon ref, e.g. "set:rocket" or a brand/logo ref like "brand:github" (#298). See also: get_started section "ICONS" for the full catalog. A raw emoji (e.g. "📁") still works for backward compatibility with older data, but is not the preferred form.

tools.name: update_folder
tools.description: Rename a folder, change its icon, or move it up/down the sidebar with `position`.

icon.description: A curated icon ref, e.g. "set:rocket" or a brand/logo ref like "brand:github" (#298). See also: get_started section "ICONS" for the full catalog. A raw emoji (e.g. "📁") still works for backward compatibility with older data, but is not the preferred form.

tools.name: delete_folder
tools.description: Remove a sidebar folder. Its contents are NOT deleted — documents, databases and views inside it fall back to the space root. That makes this the safe way to undo a grouping you got wrong.

tools.name: list_space_groups
tools.description: The workspace's sidebar groups — a presentational tier above spaces, distinct from list_folders (which groups things INSIDE one space). These are the existing groups a space can be filed under, instead of a near-duplicate being invented.

tools.name: create_space_group
tools.description: Add a presentational sidebar group. A space joins it through update_space's `group` param.

color.description: CSS colour for the group's letter-mark avatar.

tools.name: update_space_group
tools.description: Rename a group, change its colour, or move it up/down the sidebar with `position`.

tools.name: delete_space_group
tools.description: Remove a sidebar group. Its spaces are NOT deleted — they fall back to the ungrouped list. That makes this the safe way to undo a grouping you got wrong.

tools.name: create_relation
tools.description: Link two databases with a relation field on each side. one_to_many: each record in `database` links to ONE record in `related_database`, and each related record gets MANY back — e.g. database=Tasks, related_database=Projects means each task has one project and each project has many tasks. many_to_many: both sides link to many. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_relation"]

database.description: The "many" side for one_to_many (e.g. tasks). Same as related_database for a self-relation.

related_database.description: The "one" / parent side (e.g. projects). Same as database for a self-relation.

field_name.description: Relation field name on `database` — e.g. "Blocked by". Default: the related database name, or Parent/Related for a self-relation.

reverse_field_name.description: Inverse field name on `related_database` — e.g. "Blocks". Default: this database name, or Sub-items/Related to for a self-relation. Must differ from field_name on a self-relation.

tools.name: list_relations
tools.description: The whole relation graph of a workspace in one call — what is connected to what, one entry per relation with both sides resolved (database and field name on each). Useful for structural work: adding a field, moving a database, planning a migration, or answering "what would break if I deleted this". [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_relations"]

space.description: Only relations touching this space (name, slug, or id).

database.description: Only relations touching this database (name, qualified slug, or id).

tools.name: get_relation
tools.description: A relation's configuration: both sides, its cardinality, its auto-link rules if any, and the COMPARABLE FIELDS on each side. Those are the fields set_auto_link accepts; a pairing outside them is rejected by the server.

relation.description: The relation FIELD on this database (name or api_name), or a relation id.

tools.name: set_auto_link
tools.description: Teach a relation to link itself: give it field pairs, and a record on one side links to a record on the other whenever ALL the pairs match — e.g. this database's `customer_email` equals the target's `email`. Setting a rule does NOT link anything that already exists (run_auto_link links existing records). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES set_auto_link"]

relation.description: The relation FIELD on this database (name or api_name), or a relation id.

conditions.description: 1–5 field pairs. field_a is on THIS database, field_b on the target. Names or ids.

tools.name: run_auto_link
tools.description: Apply a relation's auto-link rules to the records that already exist, and return a summary of what got linked. It pays for itself after an import: create_records writes 100 rows in one call and this links them in one more, replacing a hundred link_records calls. Needs a rule to be set (set_auto_link).

relation.description: The relation FIELD on this database (name or api_name), or a relation id.

tools.name: find_workflow_candidates
tools.description: Scan every database you can read for a single-select that looks like its lifecycle (a status column), and report which databases already have a workflow field. Read-only. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES find_workflow_candidates"]

tools.name: nominate_workflows
tools.description: Convert chosen single-selects to the workflow field type, one per database, through the same per-field conversion the field editor uses (option ids and every record value are preserved). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES nominate_workflows"]

database.description: Database name or id.

field.description: The select field: display name, api_name or id.

dry_run.description: Default true. Pass false to actually convert.

tools.name: convert_user_field_to_members_relation
tools.description: Convert a person field (assignee, owner, reviewer...) into a real relation to the Members database, so the person is a linkable record rather than a bare id. THIS IS A DRY RUN BY DEFAULT and changes nothing until dry_run: false is passed (the dry-run result previews what applying would do). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES convert_user_field_to_members_relation"]

field.description: The user field: display name, api_name or id.

dry_run.description: Default true. Pass false to actually convert.

tools.name: convert_members_relation_to_user_field
tools.description: The reverse of convert_user_field_to_members_relation: turn a relation to the Members database back into a person field. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES convert_members_relation_to_user_field"]

field.description: The relation field pointing at Members: display name, api_name or id.

dry_run.description: Default true. Pass false to actually convert.

confirm_dependents.description: Pass true to accept removing lookup/rollup fields built on the relation.

tools.name: find_select_drift
tools.description: Find records that LOOK linked and are not: children whose select-field label matches a parent record's title, but which carry no actual link. This is the residue of a workspace that used a select column before it had a relation — the labels still read correctly to a human while every rollup, filter and linked view silently misses them. Reports only; fix_select_drift does the linking.

relation.description: The relation FIELD on this database (name or api_name), or a relation id.

record.description: The PARENT record (uuid or public number) to check for drifted children.

tools.name: fix_select_drift
tools.description: Link every currently-drifted child to the parent, in one call. find_select_drift lists them. This writes links to records the caller has not named individually, and the match is made on a label.

record.description: The PARENT record (uuid or public number).

tools.name: delete_relation
tools.description: Delete a relation by its id (from a describe_database relation field or a prior create_relation), removing both fields and all links.

tools.name: list_installed_packs
tools.description: What is already installed in this workspace, with the install id uninstall_pack needs. Installing a pack a workspace already has (install_pack) creates a second copy of its databases, which reads to the user as the agent duplicating their schema; this list shows what is already installed.

tools.name: uninstall_pack
tools.description: Remove a tracked pack install. The install id comes from list_installed_packs (it is the INSTALL, not the pack slug). Uninstalling reaches the databases the pack created, and any records a person has since put in them are the part they will miss.

confirm.description: Must be true — this removes schema the workspace may now be using.

tools.name: export_pack
tools.description: Turn part of this workspace into a pack manifest — the installable form of a schema you just built. Creates nothing; it hands back the manifest. An agent that a rule runs (`run_agent`) is exported with the pack and the rule names it by `$agent:<name>` ref, never by id, so the schedule survives a re-install. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES export_pack"]

databases.description: Databases to include (name, qualified slug, or id). Omit for the workspace default slice.

space.description: Limit the export to one space.

tools.name: browse_pack_marketplace
tools.description: Community-published packs, as opposed to list_packs' built-in gallery. Pass `pack` for one pack's manifest, changelog and versions. Someone may already have modelled the thing being asked for.

pack.description: Marketplace pack slug. Omit to list them all.

tools.name: list_pack_submissions
tools.description: This workspace's marketplace submissions and where each stands in review. Read-only: submitting a pack is a publishing act and is not available here — see the note in coverage.ts.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Starter templates — smaller than a pack: a single database shape, or a space with a few. Each is a modelled answer for an ordinary shape (a CRM, a content calendar); apply_template creates one in a single call.

tools.name: list_record_templates
tools.description: A database's record templates (ticket #1218): name, preset field values keyed by api_name, and a Markdown body with its sections. Packs ship some (Dev Tracker: Bug, Feature, Improvement for Issues). NOT list_templates, which lists starter database shapes. create_record_from_template makes a record from one.

tools.name: create_record_template
tools.description: Make a record template in a database. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_record_template"]

description.description: One line saying when to pick this template.

values.description: Preset field values keyed by api_name. Ignored with from_record.

body.description: The description the record starts with, as Markdown (use ## headings for sections). Ignored with from_record.

from_record.description: Record uuid or public number to save as a template.

tools.name: update_record_template
tools.description: Change a record template's name, description, preset values or body (send only what changes; `values` replaces the whole preset set; null clears description or body). Works on a pack-installed template too; pack uninstall then keeps it as changed.

tools.name: delete_record_template
tools.description: Delete a record template. Records already made from it are untouched.

tools.name: create_record_from_template
tools.description: Create a record pre-filled from a record template: its preset values and its body (sections included). `values` overrides a preset, usually the title. A preset that no longer fits the schema (a deleted field or option) is dropped and listed in `skipped`, the record is still made. Returns the new record.

values.description: Field values keyed by api_name that win over the template's, e.g. { name: "Login fails on Safari" }.

tools.name: apply_template
tools.description: Install a starter template. A pack-shaped template creates its own SPACE; a database-shaped one needs `space` and can be renamed on the way in. Templates seed sample records so the result is not an empty grid — remove_sample_data clears exactly those later, so applying one is not a decision anybody is stuck with.

space.description: Target space, required for a database-shaped template. Never a personal space (documents and views only, 422).

tools.name: remove_sample_data
tools.description: Delete exactly the sample records a template created, and nothing a person has added since. Sample rows left in a live database make a workspace look unfinished; this removes them once the real data is in.

tools.name: list_spaces
tools.description: List the spaces in a workspace (id, name, slug, description). Databases live in spaces; create_database takes a space name/slug.

tools.name: create_space
tools.description: Create a space (a named group of databases). Returns it with its slug, which create_database accepts to build inside it.

icon.description: A curated icon ref, e.g. "set:rocket" or a brand/logo ref like "brand:github" (#298). See also: get_started section "ICONS" for the full catalog. A raw emoji (e.g. "📁") still works for backward compatibility with older data, but is not the preferred form.

color.description: Palette colour: gray, brown, gold, orange, red, pink, purple, blue, teal, green, lime, cyan, indigo, magenta, rose. Omit on create and one is auto-assigned AT RANDOM, so databases created in a row can end up sharing a colour (two purples).

description.description: One line (max 200 chars) saying what this is FOR — read by list_* and describe_database, so it becomes context for whoever works here next. Set it when you create something: you already know the purpose at that moment.

tools.name: get_or_create_personal_space
tools.description: #520 — MY OWN personal space: private, including from admins, holds only documents and views (never databases). Idempotent — lazily provisioned on first call, returns the same space on every later call for this identity.

tools.name: update_space
tools.description: Rename a space, set its icon/colour/description, or move it into a sidebar group (#742 finding 04). Only the fields you pass change; pass null to clear colour, description, or group.

icon.description: A curated icon ref, e.g. "set:rocket" or a brand/logo ref like "brand:github" (#298). See also: get_started section "ICONS" for the full catalog. A raw emoji (e.g. "📁") still works for backward compatibility with older data, but is not the preferred form.

color.description: Palette colour: gray, brown, gold, orange, red, pink, purple, blue, teal, green, lime, cyan, indigo, magenta, rose. Omit on create and one is auto-assigned AT RANDOM, so databases created in a row can end up sharing a colour (two purples). Pass null to clear.

description.description: One line (max 200 chars) saying what this is FOR — read by list_* and describe_database, so it becomes context for whoever works here next. Set it when you create something: you already know the purpose at that moment. Pass null to clear.

group.description: Group name or id (from list_space_groups) to file this space under. Pass null to ungroup it.

restricted.description: Admin only. true = the space is visible only to people holding a grant on it (admins always see it); false = open again. A restricted database inside an open space is not opened by a space grant — it needs its own grant. Not allowed on personal spaces or system databases.

tools.name: delete_space
tools.description: #453/#37 — soft delete: the space, every database and record inside it. Recoverable via restore_space (see list_spaces_trash) as long as it stays undone — this tool does not warn "irreversible" the way it used to, because it no longer is one. Guardrail: `confirm` must equal the space name exactly, the same rule delete_database enforces for a smaller action. An empty space needs no confirm.

confirm.description: Must equal the space name exactly. Required when the space still holds databases.

tools.name: list_spaces_trash
tools.description: #37 — deleted spaces in this workspace. A deleted space no longer resolves by name anywhere else, so the ids restore_space takes are found here.

tools.name: restore_space
tools.description: #37 — bring a deleted space back, along with every database (and its fields/records/views) that was deleted WITH it (see list_spaces_trash for the id). A database independently deleted BEFORE the space was deleted stays in trash — restore that separately via restore_database.

space.description: Space id (from list_spaces_trash) — a deleted space has no live name/slug to resolve by.

tools.name: update_workspace
tools.description: Rename the workspace, set its description, or set the logo/accent colour shown on the public portal page (#539) — the top-level "what this company is doing here" line that list_workspaces returns, or an agency's own brand on the pages it shares with clients. Only the fields you pass change.

description.description: One line (max 200 chars) saying what this is FOR — read by list_* and describe_database, so it becomes context for whoever works here next. Set it when you create something: you already know the purpose at that moment. Pass null to clear.

portal_logo_url.description: Logo shown on the public portal page. Must be an https:// URL. Pass null to clear.

portal_accent_color.description: Accent colour for the public portal page, as a 6-digit hex like "#3366ff". Pass null to clear.

tools.name: delete_database
tools.description: #453/#37 — soft delete: the database and all its records. Recoverable via restore_database (see list_databases_trash), unless sever_relations is set — that part IS irreversible (it hard-deletes the relation and its paired field on the other database, along with every link). Guardrail: `confirm` must equal the database name exactly.

confirm.description: Must equal the database name exactly.

tools.name: list_databases_trash
tools.description: #37 — deleted databases in this workspace. A deleted database no longer resolves by name anywhere else, so the ids restore_database takes are found here.

tools.name: restore_database
tools.description: #37 — bring a deleted database back, along with whatever fields/records/views were deleted with it (see list_databases_trash for the id). A record independently trashed BEFORE the database was deleted stays in trash — restore that separately via restore_records.

database.description: Database id (from list_databases_trash) — a deleted database has no live name/slug to resolve by.

tools.name: update_database
tools.description: Rename a database, set its icon, colour or description, or move it to another space. The api_slug is stable (rename does not change the ref). Only the fields you pass change; pass null to clear colour or description.

icon.description: A curated icon ref, e.g. "set:rocket" or a brand/logo ref like "brand:github" (#298). See also: get_started section "ICONS" for the full catalog. A raw emoji (e.g. "📁") still works for backward compatibility with older data, but is not the preferred form.

color.description: Palette colour: gray, brown, gold, orange, red, pink, purple, blue, teal, green, lime, cyan, indigo, magenta, rose. Omit on create and one is auto-assigned AT RANDOM, so databases created in a row can end up sharing a colour (two purples). Pass null to clear.

description.description: One line (max 200 chars) saying what this is FOR — read by list_* and describe_database, so it becomes context for whoever works here next. Set it when you create something: you already know the purpose at that moment. Pass null to clear.

move_to_space.description: Space name or slug to move the database into. Never a personal space: those hold documents and views only (422).
