tools.name: duplicate_database
tools.description: Copy a database's schema — fields (including select/multi-select/workflow options with their colours), views and self-relations — into a new, fully independent database in the same space. Formulas and filtered views keep working in the copy (api_names are preserved; only internal ids are fresh). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES duplicate_database"]

name.description: Name for the copy. Defaults to "<source> copy", disambiguated if that name is taken.

include_records.description: Copy up to 50 records along with the schema. Default false (schema only).

tools.name: change_field_type
tools.description: Convert a field to a different type (e.g. text → select). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES change_field_type"]

tools.name: reorder_fields
tools.description: Set the order of fields in a database. Pass the field names (or api_names) in the desired order; any omitted stay after the ordered ones.

tools.name: reorder_options
tools.description: Set the order of a select / multi_select / workflow field's options. Pass option LABELS (or ids) in the desired order; any you leave out keep their relative order after the ones you name. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES reorder_options"]

order.description: Option labels (or ids) in the desired order.

tools.name: reorder_views
tools.description: Set the order of views in a database. Pass the view names in the desired order.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: List the skills visible to the caller in a workspace: the caller's own, every skill shared with the workspace, every public one, and any `members` skill that names the caller. `visibility` says which tier each is: personal ("Only me"), members (named people), shared (the workspace), public (anyone with the link). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_skills"]

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Read one skill in full, including its `instructions` — which list_skills omits to keep the catalog small. update_skill replaces a field WHOLE, so editing instructions means sending the full new text; the current text is returned here, as is the full text of a skill someone else wrote.

tools.name: list_skill_templates
tools.description: The starter scaffolds a skill can be authored from — each a complete, worked example of the five fields (name, description, when_to_use, instructions, examples). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_skill_templates"]

tools.name: create_skill
tools.description: Save a reusable skill: a named instruction bundle that you or another agent can run later with run_skill (list_skill_templates shows a worked example). The skill is recorded as authored by an agent, and unless `visibility: "personal"` is passed it is created SHARED with the whole workspace (every member's AI can find and run it), so teammates' AI will follow its text as instructions. `visibility: "members"` (with `members`) shares with only the named people; `public` can be requested, but that only raises an approval a person must give in the app Inbox and it is never public until they do. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_skill"]

name.description: Short, specific name — how a person will pick it out of a list. Max 100 chars.

description.description: One or two sentences on what it does. Max 500 chars.

when_to_use.description: The trigger, in the words someone would use when they need it — this is what a future agent matches against, so "when a lead lands and needs a first reply drafted" beats "for leads". Max 1000 chars.

instructions.description: The actual procedure, as numbered steps, read later by someone with NO memory of this session: it names the databases and fields explicitly and says what NOT to do (invent a price, send anything). Max 20000 chars.

examples.description: Worked input→output pairs. One good example does more than a paragraph of clarification. Max 20.

from_template.description: Template id from list_skill_templates, recorded as provenance.

visibility.description: Who can see it: `shared` (the whole workspace; the default), `personal` (only the token owner), `members` (only the people in `members`, plus you), or `public` (anyone with a link). `public` is NOT applied by this call: it raises an approval that a PERSON must give in the app Inbox; until then the skill stays as it was.

members.description: With visibility `members`: who can see it, as user ids from list_members or exact names. On update this REPLACES the whole set, so adding or removing someone means sending the full new list (get_skill returns the current one). Everyone not named gets nothing, not even a hint the skill exists.

tools.name: update_skill
tools.description: Edit a skill you own (each field passed REPLACES that field whole, and get_skill returns the current text; editing someone else's skill is refused). Pass `visibility` to move it between `personal`, `members` (only the people in `members`; that list REPLACES the whole set), `shared` (the whole workspace) and `public` (only raises an approval a person must give in the app Inbox). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES update_skill"]

instructions.description: Replaces the whole procedure (get_skill returns the current one).

version.description: Semver, e.g. "1.1.0". Bump it when you change the procedure.

visibility.description: Who can see it: `shared` (the whole workspace; the default), `personal` (only the token owner), `members` (only the people in `members`, plus you), or `public` (anyone with a link). `public` is NOT applied by this call: it raises an approval that a PERSON must give in the app Inbox; until then the skill stays as it was.

members.description: With visibility `members`: who can see it, as user ids from list_members or exact names. On update this REPLACES the whole set, so adding or removing someone means sending the full new list (get_skill returns the current one). Everyone not named gets nothing, not even a hint the skill exists.

tools.name: delete_skill
tools.description: Delete a skill you own. Unlike a record there is no trash and no 30-day window — a skill is gone. Editing its when_to_use stops it being suggested without destroying it. Deleting someone else's is refused even if you can see it.

confirm.description: Must be true. The guard exists because this is unrecoverable and a name can resolve by partial match.

tools.name: export_skill
tools.description: Render a skill as portable instructions that mean the same thing pasted into a different tool: `markdown` (plain prose), `claude_skill` (a SKILL.md with name/description frontmatter, the on-disk Agent Skills convention), or `chatgpt` (custom-instructions shaped). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES export_skill"]

tools.name: import_skill
tools.description: Bring a SKILL.md (or a Markdown export from StoryOS) in as a skill. It ALWAYS returns a KEPT/DROPPED report first, and by default creates nothing: `kept` lists what landed in which StoryOS field, `dropped` lists every part of the file StoryOS has no field for (with the reason — e.g. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES import_skill"]

content.description: The full text of the SKILL.md, including any frontmatter.

create.description: Default false = preview only. true = write the skill after reporting.

overrides.description: Fields to supply or replace — covers what the report lists under `missing`.

tools.name: run_skill
tools.description: Run a saved skill by name or id (from list_skills). This call invokes NO model: it resolves the skill's instructions and records the run, and YOU — the connected AI, on your own subscription, never metered — are the one who carries out `instructions` against `inputs`. An agent applies a skill when the skill is named in that agent's Skills field. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES run_skill"]

inputs.description: Free-form inputs this run should apply the skill to — returned alongside the instructions for you to act on, not sent to the API.

tools.name: get_agents
tools.description: Whether this workspace has the Agentic OS provisioned, and a summary of its three system databases: Agents (agentic_os/agents), Agent runs (agentic_os/runs, the agent executions; not the Automation runs page, which is automation rule runs) and Triggers (agentic_os/agent_triggers). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_agents"]

tools.name: get_agent_scope
tools.description: Ticket #1195 — the databases an agent can work in, resolved NOW: the databases named in its `target_databases` plus every USER database in the spaces named in its `target_spaces` (a system database such as Members is never covered by a space, only by being named; a database added to a target space later is included on the next call, nothing is expanded at hire), narrowed to what the agent's manager can open. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_agent_scope"]

agent.description: The agent record's uuid or public number (from get_agents/query_records).

tools.name: get_agent_wake_sources
tools.description: Everything that can start an agent, from one call (ticket #1289). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_agent_wake_sources"]

agent.description: The agent record's uuid or public number (from get_agents/query_records).

tools.name: list_agent_activity
tools.description: #541 — field changes + creation events attributed to ONE agent, in a date range (default: last 30 days). "Which agent, under whose authority, at what time" — each row carries agent_id, agent_name (the name at the time of the write), source and time, but NO run id: a run is shown by get_runs / get_run. Admin only. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_agent_activity"]

agent.description: The agent record's uuid or public number (from get_agents/query_records).

from.description: ISO datetime, inclusive. Default: 30 days ago.

tools.name: setup_agents
tools.description: Provision the Agentic OS space and its three system databases: Agents (agentic_os/agents), Agent runs (agentic_os/runs) and Triggers (agentic_os/agent_triggers). Idempotent — safe to call when it already exists, which is why get_agents and this can be used together without a check-then-act race. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES setup_agents"]

tools.name: run_agent
tools.description: Run an agent by hand and get back its Run record, including the step log. Works with no model configured — the run class is stamped at dispatch and a runtime error lands as a Failed run rather than an error here, so the absence of an exception does not mean the run succeeded; the returned run says. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES run_agent"]

agent.description: The agent record's uuid or public number (from the Agents database).

tools.name: delegate_to_agent
tools.description: Hand one record to an agent: it runs with that record as its context and posts its outcome back ON the record as a comment, with a link to the full Run. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES delegate_to_agent"]

agent.description: The agent record's uuid or public number.

database.description: Database holding the record to delegate.

tools.name: create_agent_trigger
tools.description: Fire an agent whenever a record reaches a given state (or, with relation_field instead of a state, whenever a record's relation field is linked to the agent). By default it starts the agent by itself, so it fits an agent meant to run on its own. A run is not held for approval as a whole: outward actions its writes set off (email, Slack, webhook, HTTP, social post) are staged for a person, with one exception: a send_email whose recipients (to and cc) are all active workspace members runs as configured unless the agent's approval_policy lists email. human_gate:true means it NEVER fires by itself (a person starts each run). The state field must be a select/workflow and the option one of its own (describe_database shows them). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_agent_trigger"]

agent.description: The agent record's uuid or public number.

database.description: The database whose state changes should fire the agent.

state_field.description: State binding: the select/workflow field to watch (name, api_name, or id).

state.description: State binding: the option that fires it — the human label, e.g. "New".

relation_field.description: Relation binding (instead of state_field + state): a relation field on the database that points at the Agents database, e.g. "Next". Linking it to the agent wakes the agent (#1130).

human_gate.description: true = "ask me before each run": this trigger never starts a run by itself; a person starts each run (ADR-0010). The default is false: the agent wakes by itself. Not the same as holding the agent's writes for approval.

tools.name: get_staged_action
tools.description: What a parked run is waiting to do, plus its step log — or null if it is not waiting. READ-ONLY, and deliberately: approving or rejecting is human-only (ADR-0010), and no tool here can do it. This exists so an agent can tell a person exactly what they are being asked to decide, which is the opposite of deciding for them. Point them at the Inbox to approve.

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: One run in full: what triggered it, each action with its attempts and artifacts, and its approval linkage. get_runs lists them; this is the one to read when something did not do what was expected, because the per-action attempt log is where the reason lives.

tools.name: get_run_quota
tools.description: This month's automation-run usage against the plan allowance, with a projection of where the pace lands. A rule that fires on every record change can look harmless and still be the one that exhausts the month.

tools.name: rerun_run
tools.description: Run the SAME rule once more on the SAME trigger record, as a NEW run: the original run and everything it did are left as they were. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES rerun_run"]

tools.name: list_ai_connections
tools.description: The AI clients the CALLING person has connected, as one list: hosted-MCP OAuth clients (Claude, ChatGPT, ...) and personal access tokens, each with its `reaches`: all_workspaces, one_workspace, needs_reconnect or this_workspace. An OAuth connection has no access level of its own: it acts as the person, so their workspace role and grants decide what it can do. A personal access token (connected: token) DOES carry a scope, read, write or admin, set when it was created and enforced on every call: a read token is refused a write. Lists only the caller's own connections; read-only (disconnecting is a person's act in Settings). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_ai_connections"]

tools.name: rerun_action
tools.description: Retry ONE failed action from a run, with its original frozen inputs — so it repeats what it was actually asked to do, not what the record says now. It is for after the cause is fixed (a bad credential, a missing field). The action's index comes from get_run. It re-runs a single action, never the whole run (rerun_run covers the whole run).

action_index.description: The failed action's index, from get_run.

tools.name: duplicate_view
tools.description: Copy a view, with its filters, sorts, grouping and column layout. The fastest way to make a variant of something that already works — build the board once, duplicate it, then change the one thing that differs. Cheaper and safer than rebuilding a config by hand, which is where a filter gets subtly mistyped.

name.description: Name for the copy. Defaults to the API's own "… copy".

tools.name: set_default_view
tools.description: Choose which view people land on when they open this database. This changes what EVERY member sees, unlike a personal filter.

tools.name: publish_view
tools.description: Turn a view you own privately (made with create_personal_view) into an ordinary shared view everyone with access to the database can see. One-way (personal-space.md) — the way back is copy_view_to_personal_space, an independent fork, never an un-publish. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES publish_view"]

view.description: Your personal view's name or id (from list_personal_views).

tools.name: copy_view_to_personal_space
tools.description: Fork a shared view into your own private copy — an independent clone of its config, never synced back (personal-space.md's answer to "publishing is one-way"). Reconfiguring either view afterward never touches the other.

view.description: The shared view to copy (from describe_database).

tools.name: share_view
tools.description: Publish a saved view (or update an already-published one's allowlist) to a public, unauthenticated read-only link for clients or stakeholders — the API half only; there is no web page for the link yet. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES share_view"]

visible_field_api_names.description: Field api_names to expose. Omit for the view's own non-hidden fields. A rollup/formula/lookup must be named here explicitly or it never appears.

include_relation_api_names.description: Relation field api_names allowed to travel, as id/title/number chips only. Omit or [] = no related data leaves.

indexable.description: Allow search engines to index the link. Default false (noindex).

tools.name: unshare_view
tools.description: Take a published view back offline. The link 404s immediately — no cache, no grace window.

tools.name: get_personal_filter
tools.description: The extra filter the CALLING identity has layered on a view, on top of what everyone else sees, or null if none. A personal filter is invisible to teammates by design, so "my board is empty and yours isn't" usually means this.

tools.name: set_personal_filter
tools.description: Narrow a view for YOURSELF only, leaving what teammates see untouched — "the team board, but just my rows". Pass clear:true to remove it. It writes for the identity this token belongs to and cannot filter anyone else's screen; update_view changes the view for everyone. Filter syntax is identical to query_records.

filter.description: A query_records-style filter. Omit with clear:true.

tools.name: get_personal_collection_filter
tools.description: The extra filter the CALLING identity has layered on a record page's embedded relation collection (the linked-records list under a relation field), on top of what everyone else sees, or null if none. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_personal_collection_filter"]

tools.name: set_personal_collection_filter
tools.description: Narrow a record page's embedded relation collection for YOURSELF only, leaving what teammates see untouched — same idea as set_personal_filter but for a field's collection widget rather than a saved view. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES set_personal_collection_filter"]

filter.description: A query_records-style filter, evaluated against the TARGET database. Omit with clear:true.

clear.description: Remove your entire personal override for this collection (filter, sort, color, columns).

tools.name: list_space_views
tools.description: Views that belong to a SPACE rather than a database — dashboards that pull from several databases at once, and the ones that appear in the sidebar tree. describe_database only ever shows a database's own views, so these are invisible from there. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_space_views"]

tools.name: list_personal_views
tools.description: #551 — every PERSONAL view I own, across the whole workspace (not scoped to one database or space). A personal view is invisible to everyone else, including admins, and is only otherwise reachable per-database — this is the one call that lists all of mine at once, for a workspace-wide 'my personal views' surface.

tools.name: create_space_view
tools.description: Create a space-level DASHBOARD — the only view type that lives on a space rather than a database, because it is the only one that reads from several. It suits a "how is everything going" page; create_view covers anything scoped to one database.

tools.name: get_view
tools.description: One view by id, whether it belongs to a database or a space. describe_database covers a database's own views; this tool resolves a view id from a shared link or list_space_views when it is not known whether it belongs to a database or a space.

tools.name: update_space_view
tools.description: Rename a space-level view, change its config, or MOVE a database dashboard into a space so it stops being scoped to one database. Pass `space` to move it. A database view's filters and layout are updated with update_view.

space.description: Move the view into this space (name, slug, or id).

tools.name: delete_space_view
tools.description: Delete a space-level view. Deletes the VIEW, never the records it showed — a dashboard is a lens, and removing it removes nothing underneath. A database's own views are deleted with delete_view.

tools.name: list_members
tools.description: Who is in this workspace and what role they hold — the list of valid values for a `user` field, because an address that is not a member is rejected. Returns name, role and user id; the id is what a user field wants. Read-only: this cannot invite, remove, or change anyone's access. Those are human decisions and have no tool at any scope.

tools.name: list_grants
tools.description: Who can reach which spaces and databases, beyond their workspace role. When a database is missing for one person and present for another, a grant, or its absence, is usually the answer. Read-only: granting and revoking are human decisions.

user.description: Narrow to one user id (from list_members).

tools.name: list_audit_log
tools.description: #454 — "who changed or deleted what, and when" across every user in the workspace, filterable by actor/entity/date range (default: last 30 days). Reads the SAME activity_events/record_field_changes tables list_comments/get_history read per-record, just workspace-wide. A removed member still appears by name (the no-FK design). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_audit_log"]

actor.description: Narrow to one user id (from list_members).

entity.description: Narrow to one record, space, database or view id.

type.description: #1059 — narrow to event types, comma-separated, e.g. "space.deleted,database.deleted,view.deleted,database.restricted". Omit for everything.

from.description: ISO datetime, inclusive. Default: 30 days ago.

source.description: #934 — narrow to actions by these kinds of actor, comma-separated: human, agent, automation, mcp (e.g. "agent,mcp" for what agents did). Each event row also carries credential_id (which token did it) and agent_id/agent_name.

tools.name: list_invites
tools.description: Invitations sent but not yet accepted. A colleague who "is not in the workspace" may simply not have clicked the link yet, which is a different problem with a different fix. A revoked invite is not pending and is not listed. Read-only: inviting and revoking are human decisions.

tools.name: get_my_work
tools.description: The surfaces a person actually opens, for the identity this token belongs to, as `kind`: "assigned" (default; open records assigned to them, with who set them and when), "created", "assigned_by_me", "waiting" (approvals they can decide, each with `rule_label` (the automation rule asking: its name if you may read that database's automations, else "A rule in <database>") and unanswered mentions), "recent", "favorites". Finished records are never returned; lists are per database, at most 50 rows each, with an exact `total` and `truncated: true` when cut, so a count is never the size of one page. Your own surfaces only. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_my_work"]

tools.name: set_favorite
tools.description: Star a record or database for the calling identity, or remove a star. Starring is how a person finds something again; an unstarred new database is one they have to go looking for. Stars are per-person: this cannot star anything for a teammate.

target.description: Database name/slug/id, or a record uuid.

database.description: Required when target_type is "record" and `target` is a public number.

starred.description: true (default) to star, false to unstar.

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description: What is waiting for the identity this token belongs to — assignments, mentions, comments, state changes and approval requests, newest first. This is the "what should I look at" question, and it is the one an agent could not answer before: notify existed, reading did not. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_notifications"]

unread_only.description: Only what has not been read yet.

archived.description: Show the archived pile instead of the inbox.

tools.name: get_unread_count
tools.description: How many unread notifications the calling identity has — one number, no pagination. Cheaper than list_notifications when the question is only "is there anything waiting", e.g. at the start of a session.

tools.name: mark_notifications
tools.description: Mark notifications read, or archive them, for the calling identity only. Pass `all: true` with action "read" to clear the whole inbox at once. It is the person's own inbox, and a notification archived by an agent is one they never saw; reading and reporting leave it as it was.

all.description: With action "read" only: mark everything read.

tools.name: list_approvals
tools.description: MN-255: list this workspace's require_approval gate items (pending/approved/rejected/expired) — the preview text, status and approver of each, and the automation rule asking: `rule_label` is its current name when you may read that database's automations (then `rule_id`/`rule_name` are set too), else a neutral "A rule in <database>" with `rule_id`/`rule_name` null; all three null when no rule wrote it (an agent proposal) or the rule was deleted. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_approvals"]

status.description: Filter by status; omit for all.

tools.name: list_action_gates
tools.description: #542: this workspace's declared gate policies over an action class (currently only "delete_records") — scope (workspace/space/database), enabled, and who approves. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_action_gates"]

tools.name: list_agent_write_gates
tools.description: #1104: the gates that hold an agent's record create and/or update for a person's approval, instead of applying it. Each has the agent_id (an Agents-database record), operations (create, update), database_id (null = every database), fields (null = any write; otherwise only a write that touches one of those api_names) and enabled. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_agent_write_gates"]

agent_id.description: Limit to one agent (its record uuid).

tools.name: list_runners
tools.description: The StoryOS Runners YOU own (a Runner is a program on your own computer that wakes your agents inside your own Claude Code, on your own subscription), each with status, connection (online, offline, paused, outdated, tool_missing, revoked), working hours, reserve and hold. An agent set to "Your own AI" with no active, online Runner waits, which is the usual reason an agent is not running. Only your own, never a colleague's. Adding or changing a Runner is done by a person in StoryOS (Settings, Runners); there is deliberately no tool for it. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_runners"]

tools.name: list_agent_wakes
tools.description: The queue behind agents that run on your own AI through a Runner: which agent was woken about which record, why (reason), how many events merged into it (coalesced_count) and ONE derived run_state, computed by the server and not meant to be recomputed (needs_approval, running, done, failed, canceled, waiting_for_runner, runner_offline, waiting_for_limit, waiting_for_hours, waiting_for_reserve, waiting_for_budget, waiting_for_turn). Filter with agent and record. Only wakes whose record and agent you can read are listed. Waking, claiming and finishing a wake are not tools. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_agent_wakes"]

agent.description: The agent record's uuid (from the Agents database).

record.description: A record uuid, or its public number when `database` is given.

database.description: The database of `record`, only needed when `record` is a public number.

tools.name: get_agent_wake_summary
tools.description: #1130: how much work is waiting for agents that run on your own AI. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_agent_wake_summary"]

tools.name: list_agent_catch_up
tools.description: ticket #1224: the records already sitting in an agent's trigger state(s) that no wake was ever made for, BY NAME (the list behind `catch_up` in get_agent_wake_summary). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_agent_catch_up"]

agent.description: The agent record's uuid (from the Agents database; get_agent_wake_summary shows it).

offset.description: Skip this many, to page through when truncated is true.

tools.name: get_agent_budget
tools.description: One agent's monthly token budget and run cap and what it has used this UTC month, counted from its Run records (state: unlimited, ok, warning, paused, not_measured). `tokens.used` is null, never 0, when the runs' tool reported no usage, and a partial total is a lower bound ("at least"). The numbers are measured, not estimates. A budget is raised with update_record on the agent's record (a person can; an agent cannot change its own). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_agent_budget"]

agent.description: The agent record's uuid (from the Agents database; list_agent_wakes and get_agent_wake_summary show it).

tools.name: list_validation_rules
tools.description: #231: the validation rules on a database. A rule REFUSES a record write (yours included: there is no bypass for any writer) when its condition is not met, and returns the rule's own message (these are the rules behind a refused write). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_validation_rules"]

tools.name: get_validation_rule_violations
tools.description: #231: the stored records that ALREADY break a validation rule (a rule only fires when a field it references changes, so existing violations persist and are otherwise invisible). It reports on data quality and finds records to fix; fixing one is an ordinary update. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_validation_rule_violations"]

tools.name: get_runs
tools.description: MN-264: this is how you answer "why didn't my automation fire / post go out?" — every automation rule run in the workspace, newest first, with status (ok = Succeeded, error = Failed, running, skipped, skipped_quota = Skipped (quota), awaiting_approval = at least one action is waiting for a person to approve it; awaiting_approval_count says how many), the triggering record, and a per-action summary (kind + status of each external action attempted). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_runs"]

status.description: Filter by status; omit for all.

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: The accounts already connected to this workspace — id, provider, a human name, status, scopes and recent health (last_ok_at, error_count_24h). NO credential or token is ever included; auth material never leaves the app. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_connections"]

tools.name: list_connection_providers
tools.description: The catalog of provider TYPES this StoryOS instance can connect (Slack, GitHub, a raw API key, etc.) — id, label, auth_kind, its access `tier`, and whether it is actually connectable RIGHT NOW on this deployment (`availability`: connectable / operator_config — a self-managed operator has not set the env var yet / cloud_only — hosted-only, off here). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_connection_providers"]

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: The scheduled syncs feeding this database from an external provider — provider, schedule, status, field_mapping, connection_id and last_sync_at for each. It diagnoses data freshness ("is this database still syncing?"). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_sources"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

tools.name: list_source_providers
tools.description: What this database can sync FROM: the provider catalog — each entry's `id` (the `provider_source` value create_source needs, e.g. "youtube.comments"), the `connection_provider` its connection must be, its `config_schema`, and `supports_discover`. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_source_providers"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id — the sync TARGET.

tools.name: list_youtube_channels
tools.description: The YouTube channels a connected Google account owns, as `{ id, title }`. Needed only to fill the `channel_id` config key of the youtube.* source providers — a source created against the wrong channel syncs nothing and looks healthy while doing it. Reads through to YouTube using the stored connection; creates and changes nothing. Requires a "google" connection — any other provider is rejected.

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

connection_id.description: The google connection's id. See create_source for where a connection_id comes from.

tools.name: discover_source_fields
tools.description: Ask the provider what it would actually return, and propose how to map it onto this database. CREATES NOTHING, syncs nothing, writes nothing. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES discover_source_fields"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id — the sync TARGET, whose fields the proposal maps onto.

connection_id.description: The connection to read through. See create_source for where a connection_id comes from.

config.description: Provider config (shape in list_source_providers' config_schema). Partial is fine — discovery tolerates a half-filled config.

tools.name: create_source
tools.description: Configure a scheduled sync from an external provider INTO a database, and start it running. CREDENTIALS NEVER PASS THROUGH THIS TOOL: the account is connected once in the app (Settings → Connections) and referenced by `connection_id` (from list_connections, or from list_sources). list_source_providers and discover_source_fields describe what a provider offers; field_mapping maps provider keys to this database's fields, and external_key_field (one of its targets) is what makes a re-sync update instead of duplicate. Covers field_mapping directions, conflict_policy, write_back and push approval, defaults. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_source"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id — the sync TARGET.

name.description: A human label for this source, e.g. "Shopify orders".

connection_id.description: Id of the stored connection to sync through. NOT a credential — see this tool's description for where it comes from.

field_mapping.description: { "provider_external_key": "field name or id" } for a pull-only mapping (the common case), or { "provider_external_key": { field, direction } } — direction "in" (default), "out" (push-only, never overwritten by a sync), or "both". discover_source_fields returns a proposed_field_mapping in this shape.

external_key_field.description: Field (name or id) holding the provider's stable id. Must be one of field_mapping's target fields.

config.description: Provider config; shape is in list_source_providers' config_schema. May also set conflict_policy: "external_wins" (default) | "storyos_wins" | "newest_wins".

schedule.description: Coarse cadence. Omit to get the default daily sync, or pass `recurrence` for an exact time.

recurrence.description: Exact cadence, and it wins over `schedule`: {kind:"hourly",minute} | {kind:"daily",hour,minute} | {kind:"weekly",weekday,hour,minute}.

tools.name: update_source
tools.description: Reconfigure an existing source — rename it, change its schedule, repoint its field mapping, or pause and resume it. A true patch: omitted arguments are left as they are. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES update_source"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

connection_id.description: Point the source at a different stored connection.

config.description: Replacement provider config (replaces the whole object, so changing one key means sending the current config from list_sources with that key changed). May include conflict_policy: "external_wins" (default) | "storyos_wins" | "newest_wins", write_back (required true before any "out"/"both" field_mapping entry actually pushes — see create_source's description), and require_approval_for_push (default false — holds each push as an Inbox approval instead of sending it immediately).

field_mapping.description: { "provider_external_key": "field name or id" } or { "provider_external_key": { field, direction } } (direction "in"/"out"/"both") — the COMPLETE mapping, which replaces the existing one.

external_key_field.description: Field (name or id) holding the provider's stable id.

status.description: "paused" stops the schedule without discarding the source; "active" resumes it.

tools.name: delete_source
tools.description: Stop syncing and discard the source configuration — its field mapping, schedule and sync cursor. RECORDS ARE NOT DELETED: every record the source ever created stays in the database, it simply stops being updated. The configuration itself is NOT recoverable, so `confirm` must equal the source's name exactly. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES delete_source"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

confirm.description: The source's exact name, as a guard against deleting the wrong one.

tools.name: sync_source
tools.description: Run one sync cycle immediately, ignoring the schedule. Returns that run's outcome — records fetched, created, updated, and the error if it failed. It proves a newly created source works without waiting for its schedule, and refreshes data on demand. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES sync_source"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

tools.name: list_source_runs
tools.description: The sync history for ONE source, newest first — status, when it ran, how many records it fetched/created/updated, and the error message when it failed. This is the answer to "the data looks stale" and "did my sync actually do anything": a source can sit at status active and be failing every cycle. Covers scheduled runs and sync_source runs alike.

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: The workspace's outbound webhook subscriptions — url, which events each is subscribed to, whether it is enabled, and the last delivery's status/code/error. Signing secrets are never returned here. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_webhooks"]

tools.name: get_credential
tools.description: What an API token (a "credential") could reach and when it existed: its power scope, whether it was bound to specific spaces/databases (`resource_scope`; null = unrestricted), its origin, and `revoked_at`. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES get_credential"]

tools.name: list_credential_actions
tools.description: Every action (activity event: type, record id, source, time) performed with one API token, newest first, 50 per page (pass `cursor` from `next_cursor`). Together with get_credential it answers "what could this token reach, and what did it do". Works for revoked tokens. Admin only. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_credential_actions"]

tools.name: get_activity_event
tools.description: One activity event (type, record id, source, time) and `credential_id`, the API token that performed it (null for a session, an OAuth grant, an automation, or before this was recorded). Feed the id to get_credential for what that token could reach. Admin only.

tools.name: list_webhook_deliveries
tools.description: Recent delivery ATTEMPTS for one webhook, newest first — event type, status, HTTP status_code, the error text when it failed, how many attempts it has taken and when the next retry is due. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_webhook_deliveries"]

webhook.description: Webhook id, or its exact url (from list_webhooks).

tools.name: update_webhook
tools.description: Change a webhook's url, its event subscriptions, or enable/disable it. A true patch — omitted arguments are left alone. enabled:false is the safe way to stop deliveries: it keeps the subscription and its signing secret, so it can be turned back on. delete_webhook cannot be undone. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES update_webhook"]

webhook.description: Webhook id, or its exact url (from list_webhooks).

url.description: New https endpoint on a public host.

events.description: REPLACES the whole subscription list (1–20 events), it does not add to it.

enabled.description: false pauses deliveries without discarding the subscription.

take_ownership.description: true makes YOU the webhook's owner. A webhook acts with its owner's access, so when the owner is demoted, removed or was never recorded, deliveries pause (list_webhooks shows paused_reason) until an admin does this.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Delete a webhook subscription permanently, along with its signing secret. `confirm` must equal the webhook's exact url. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES delete_webhook"]

webhook.description: Webhook id, or its exact url (from list_webhooks).

confirm.description: The webhook's exact url, as a guard against deleting the wrong subscription.

tools.name: list_automations
tools.description: #334: the automation rules on one database — each with its trigger (field/relation names resolved), condition, actions, enabled state, failure streak and last-run status (ok, error, skipped, running, or awaiting_approval when an action is waiting for a person to approve it, the same word get_runs uses). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_automations"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

tools.name: get_automation
tools.description: #334: one automation rule's full, editable definition — trigger, condition and actions with human-readable database/field/select names alongside their stable ids, plus enabled state and last-run status. update_automation accepts the same shape.

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

tools.name: create_automation
tools.description: Create an automation rule: a trigger (record_created, record_updated, record_linked, schedule, webhook_received) + an optional condition + 1-10 actions (set_values, create_record, create_records, add_comment, notify_user, update_linked, send_slack_message, send_webhook, send_email, http_request, run_agent). A rule CAN REACH OUTSIDE STORYOS: it can send real email, call any public HTTP API and post to Slack, from scheduled and triggered rules alike. run_agent works an agent on a schedule or while nobody is signed in: for an agent on Your own AI, a wake queues and runs when an active, online Runner claims it (a wake nobody serves for 7 days is cancelled). A schedule every:"minutes" below 10 is refused. Covers every trigger and action shape, templates, top-N sort/limit. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_automation"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id (the rule's home database).

trigger.description: Trigger object. See also: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_automation" for shapes. record_linked accepts direction:"link"|"unlink".

actions.description: Array of 1–10 action objects. See also: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_automation" for shapes. Each may carry its own optional `condition` (api_names).

condition.description: Optional filter AST (same shape as query_records) — the rule only runs on records that match. Not allowed on webhook_received.

approver.description: User id who approves this rule's require_approval actions (defaults to the rule owner).

sort.description: Schedule-only top-N ordering — sort keys by field api_name, same shape as query_records' sorts. Rejected on any other trigger.

limit.description: Schedule-only top-N count, capped at 200. Rejected on any other trigger.

tools.name: update_automation
tools.description: #334: edit an existing rule — rename, enable/disable, or replace its trigger / condition / actions. Every field is optional; omit what you are not changing. To disable a rule pass { enabled: false }. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES update_automation"]

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

condition.description: Replacement filter AST, or null to clear it.

approver.description: Approver user id, or null to revert to the rule owner.

sort.description: Schedule-only top-N ordering (see create_automation), or null to clear it.

limit.description: Schedule-only top-N count (see create_automation), or null to clear it.

tools.name: delete_automation
tools.description: #334: permanently delete an automation rule. Requires explicit confirmation: pass confirm=true. Reports the deleted rule's name, trigger and action summary so the caller can see exactly what was removed. Its run history goes with it.

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

confirm.description: Must be true — deleting a rule is irreversible.

tools.name: test_automation
tools.description: #684 — dry-run a rule against one record before trusting it live. Omit `action_index` to just check whether the rule's condition matches this record and see which actions WOULD run (no side effects). Pass `action_index` to actually send that one http_request action for real — everything else is not currently testable this way.

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

record.description: Record uuid or public number to test against.

action_index.description: Index into the rule's actions array — actually SENDS that http_request action. Omit for a side-effect-free condition check.

tools.name: get_automation_last_payload
tools.description: #684 — the most recent inbound payload a webhook_received rule received, and when. For mapping the sender's field names to this rule's actions before trusting it live. Never includes the rule's own hook token or secret.

database.description: Database name, api slug, or id.

tools.name: list_portal_recipients
tools.description: External parties (clients, not users) with standing access to this workspace's published portal content — no login, no seat. Read-only here.

tools.name: create_portal_recipient
tools.description: Names a new external party for the portal (#534) — never creates a user, sends no invitation, and never counts toward billable seats. Returns a signed token (#602 — id.version.hmac, not a bare opaque value); what content it can reach is not yet wired to anything (row scoping ships separately).

label.description: Display name for this recipient, e.g. a client's company name.

email.description: Optional — for your own reference, not used for delivery yet.

expires_at.description: ISO datetime. Absent = never expires. An expired token is refused the same way a revoked one is.

tools.name: revoke_portal_recipient
tools.description: Closes a recipient's access immediately — no cache, no TTL. Irreversible as a token (a new recipient would need a new token); the row itself stays for audit.

tools.name: rotate_portal_recipient
tools.description: #602 — issues a new signed token for this recipient and atomically invalidates the old one (no window where both or neither work). For a token that may have leaked while the recipient should keep access (revoke_portal_recipient, by contrast, ends access permanently).

tools.name: list_portal_activity
tools.description: #537 — "what each client actually saw and did": every recipient-scoped portal access, filterable by recipient and/or published view. served = they got content (even if a fail-closed scope left it empty — this answers "did they look", not "did they see rows"); rejected = turned away, with a reason. A revoked recipient's history survives. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES list_portal_activity"]

recipient.description: Narrow to one recipient id (from list_portal_recipients).

view.description: Narrow to one published view id.
